texts.facts: Aggrieved by the very same judgment in M.V.C.No.737/2015 dated 20.01.2017 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-II, Ballari (for short 'the Tribunal'), the appeal preferred by the insurer is on the ground of excessive compensation awarded to the claimant as being exorbitant. Appeal preferred by the claimant is founded on the premise of inadequacy of compensation. 2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal. 3. Brief facts of the case is as under: On 18.06.2015, at about 06.00 p.m. when the claimant was proceeding along with one Govinda on his TVS Star City Motorcycle, as a pillion rider from Sirigedoddi village towards Rayadurga, at that time, when they reached at Sirigedoddi village, Gummagatta Mandalam, respondent No.1, who was driving the Bolero Maxi Truck bearing Reg. No.KA-16/B-7058 came from Rayadurga side in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger to human life and safety, dashed against the motorcycle, in which the claimant was a pillion rider. Due to the impact of the accident, the claimant as well as rider of the motorcycle fell down and sustained Grade-I compound fracture of right tibia lower 1/3rd with compound fracture of 1st metatarsal with crush injury over foot. Immediately thereafter, claimant shifted to Community Health Centre, Rayadurga, where he was admitted. Thereafter, he was admitted to Sanjeevini Hospital, Ballari, where the claimant took treatment as an inpatient from 19.06.2015 to 22.06.2015. It is stated that during the course of treatment, major operation was conducted on the right leg and steel rods and plates were inserted. Pursuant to which, claimant took continuous follow up treatment with the private doctors for a long time. 4. It is stated that claimant incurred a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical and other miscellaneous expenses. It is the case of claimant that he was hale and healthy, aged about 23 years and he was doing coolie work, earning a sum of Rs.400/- per day and was contributing his earnings for the welfare of maintenance of his family. It is also stated that he is only earning member of his family and due to the accident and the injuries suffered by him, he is not in a position to either walk or work as before. It is also stated that due to the injuries suffered by him in the accident, he has lost his earning capacity as he was prior to the date of occurrence of accident. Due to the occurrence of accident and the injuries suffered, the claimant preferred claim petition claiming compensation against the respondents. M/S. Shriram General Insurance Company ... vs Palaiah @ K Pala Nayaka on 30 May, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90987655/ 3 5. On notice being issued, respondents appeared before the Tribunal and filed their detailed statement of objections inter alia denying the contentions putforth by the claimant. It is the statement of respondent No.2-owner of the offending vehicle that since his vehicle is insured with respondent No.3 and if any liability is fastened on him, the same will have to be indemnified by respondent No.3- insurer. Respondent No.3 however filed separate statement of objections inter alia denying all the contentions made by the claimant. However, it admitted the insurance policy being in force with regard to respondent No.2. However, he denied the occurrence of accident, the age, avocation of claimant and the medical expenses having incurred by the claimant and that the claim petition was bad for mis-joinder and non joinder of proper and necessary parties. So also contended that the claim made by the claimant was excessive and exorbitant and sought for dismissal of the claim petition. 6. On the basis of pleadings, the Tribunal has framed relevant issues for consideration. 7. In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the claimant got examined himself as PW.1 and also examined the doctor as PW.2 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P10. However, the respondents have not led any evidence neither have produced any material on their behalf. 8. On the basis of the material evidence both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both the parties, the Tribunal awarded total compensation of Rs.7,20,680/- to be jointly and severally paid by the respondent Nos.1 to 3 with interest @ 7% p.a. to the claimant. However, directed the 3rd respondent being the insurer to deposit the compensation amount in view of the insurance police being in force.
texts.arguments: 9. Being aggrieved by the exorbitant amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal and the erroneous calculations of disability by PW.2 and the Tribunal calculating the disability at 40%, the insurance company is in appeal challenging the same. Whereas, claimant has approached this Court, seeking enhancement of compensation on the ground of meager compensation awarded by the Tribunal. 10. It is the vehement contention of learned counsel appearing for the insurer that the Tribunal has grossly erred in not considering the material evidence on record both oral and documentary and has erred in calculating the disability to an extent of 40% without there being any reasonable basis or clinical assessment to that effect. It is further contended by the learned counsel for the Insurer that the Tribunal has committed an error in not taking into consideration the evidence of Doctor P.W.2 and has awarded disability to an extent of 40% which is highly erroneous and without any medical and clinical analysis put forth by the Doctor. It is further contended by the learned counsel that the Tribunal has awarded just and reasonable compensation on all other heads. Therefore, the question of enhancement of compensation under other heads does not arise. He further contends that the Tribunal has awarded suitable compensation based on the material evidence placed by the claimant. Therefore, enhancement sought for by the claimant in the connected appeal does not deserve to be considered as just and reasonable compensation has been awarded by the Tribunal. On these grounds, learned counsel for the Insurer seeks to allow his appeal and dismiss the appeal preferred by the claimant. M/S. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent- claimant vehemently contends that the Tribunal has committed a gross error in not appreciating the material evidence both oral and documentary and has awarded meager compensation including the assessment of income of the claimant, which is on the lower side. Learned counsel further contends that the Tribunal ought to have taken income at Rs.12,000/- per month as he was a coolie and since the claimant has undergone surgery due to serious injuries with crush injury to the right foot and fracture of his right leg. He is unable to stand, walk and climb steps up and down and perform daily routine agriculture works. The Tribunal ought to have awarded just and reasonable compensation, whereas the Tribunal has assessed the income at Rs.6,000/- per month which is on the lower side. 12. Learned counsel for the claimant further contends that the assessment made by the Doctor, P.W.2, is correct in view of the fact that the claimant has sustained Grade I compound fracture of right tibia lower 1/3rd with compound fracture of 1st metatarsal bone with crush injury to foot. It is vehement contention of the claimant that since the claimant has sustained grievous crush injury on his right foot and question of him getting back to his work and perform his normal day today activities in the agriculture field as a coolie is totally ruled out in view of the serious injuries. Therefore, it is his contention that the Doctor P.W.2 has rightly assessed the disability to n extent of 45%. The same requires to be awarded whereas the Tribunal has reduced the percentage of disability to extent of 40% which is erroneous in law. 13. Learned counsel further contends that the Tribunal has not awarded suitable compensation under the head of loss of income during treatment period so also no amount of compensation is awarded under the head of nourishment, attendant charges and extra nourishment - 10 - during period of treatment. It is also contended by learned counsel that the Tribunal has erred in not awarding future medical expenses as claimed by him in view of the fact that he is required to further undergo one more surgery for removal of implants. It is further contended that the Tribunal has grossly erred in not awarding suitable compensation under the head loss of amenities. On these grounds, he seeks to allow the appeal by enhancing the compensation and dismissing the appeal filed by the Insurer. 14. Having heard the learned counsel for the claimant and learned counsel for Insurer, the points that would arise for consideration before this Court are: "i) Whether the Tribunal has awarded exorbitant compensation? ii) Whether the claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation? It is not in dispute that the accident occurred on 18.06.2015 whiling claimant was riding the motorcycle. When the respondent No.1 being the driver of the Bolero Maxi Truck came from the M/S. Learned counsel appearing for the insurer vehemently contends that when an analysis is made by the Doctor who deposes before the Court, he has to make it on the basis of his personal interaction when the operation or having treated/the claimant he himself or by comparing the x-ray and treatment given to the claimant. In the present case on hand, the Doctor P.W.2 is not the Doctor who treated the claimant and hence he contends that the assessment of disability to an extent of 45% is on the higher side.
